newsitem.title: UK: RHODIUM DEMAND FALLS IN 1996 ON CAR MAKER CUTS-JM.
newsitem.headline: RHODIUM DEMAND FALLS IN 1996 ON CAR MAKER CUTS-JM.

text.p: Rhodium demand declined by 16,000 ounces to 458,000 ounces in 1996 as cutbacks by the car makers outweighed higher demand from the glass and chemical industries, according to the Platinum 1997 survey of the platinum group metals published by Johnson Matthey on Monday.
Johnson Matthey is the world's leading refiner of platinum group metals.
Total supply was up 40,000 ounces at 476,000 ounces with South Africa exporting 359,000 ounces, up 17,000 ounces on 1995, and Russia 110,000 ounces, up 30,000 ounces on the previous year.
Demand for the major end use in autocatalysts fell 50,000 ounces to 414,000 ounces but in North America there was a slight increase in rhodium loadings.
The U.S. Low Emission Vehicle (LEV) legislation expected later this decade could further boost rhodium's use in catalysts, the survey said.
But lower rhodium demand in North America was the major factor behind the overall fall as consumption there fell to 158,000 ounces from 224,000 ounces in 1995.

Clean air legislation in Europe was also forecast to lift rhodium demand. The switch by European car makers to palladium-based catalysts was not a factor as the rhodium loading remained intact, the survey said.
Total European demand rose 15,000 ounces in 1996 to 154,000 ounces, reflecting higher car production.
The Japanese car companies purchased slightly more rhodium last year than in 1995 indicating that they have worked down the inventories built up earlier in the decade.
Even so, Japanese imports in total grew only 13,000 ounces to 72,000 ounces. South Korean demand was also up.
"We expect further growth in consumption in 1997 in line with rising car production and adoption of catalystc converters on cars in Malaysia," the survey said.
Demand from Latin American car makers rose sharply, principally in Mexico where production is aimed at sales in the United States.
Further increases are forecast for 1997 following tighter emission control legislation in Brazil and Mexico and the introduction of emission laws in Argentina.
Speculative selling forced rhodium prices to a 23-year low of $230 per ounce last December but they have recovered about $50 since.
